tools_used: WebFetch (reply brief PDF from supremecourt.gov) plus local PDF text extraction
helpful: Full petition and BIO text, including the published opinion below, carried nearly the whole forecast.
context.json's band matching the statpack table's salience version made the anchor a single pooled figure.
The snapshot's document links let me reach the reply brief filed two days ago.
gaps: The reply brief (on the snapshot since Sep 15) was not provisioned under record/documents/; a reply filed before the conference is routinely the freshest signal on a CFR'd petition.
WebFetch cannot read PDFs; a fetch-and-extract path for supremecourt.gov docket PDFs would remove a manual step.
fedcourts query has no topic or text filter on SCOTUS rows, so it cannot surface priors on the same question presented.
CourtListener's SCOTUS docket index returned nothing for the statute's phrase, so I could not verify prior denials of comparable post-Ramos petitions.
No published cut for grant rate conditional on a call for a response after a waiver, the strongest single signal here (the band folds it in but does not isolate it).
notes: Five retrieval calls in total (one corpus query, three MCP searches, one web fetch), well inside budget.
